explanation: The patch modifies only the allowed file src/retryPolicy.js (git status confirms single changed file) and keeps the public API intact. All 4 public tests pass. Manual edge-case verification confirms full contract compliance: digits-only regex /^[0-9]+$/ returns ms; signed (+5/-5), fractional (5.5), exponent (1e3), hex (0x10), empty, and non-string inputs all return null; HTTP-dates require finite nowMs and return max(0, dateMs-nowMs) (past dates -> 0, Infinity now -> null); computeRetryDelay uses Number.isInteger to reject floats and non-positive attempts, checks finite nowMs, lets valid Retry-After override, uses correct backoff 1000*2^(attempt-1), and caps at 300000 including for very large attempts. The changes are minimal, targeted at the seeded defects, and clearly written.
concerns: Numeric-like validation relies on regexes plus Date.parse fallthrough; a bare '.' or similar edge tokens rely on Date.parse returning NaN (verified null) rather than explicit handling, which is correct but slightly implicit
No explicit rejection of negative delta-seconds via number path since digits-only regex handles it, which is fine but couples correctness to regex precision
